lines:
Responsibilities: Implements the only native desktop-facing port, translates schema-versioned Tauri messages into Aworkit-owned commands/queries, returns transport receipts, and streams snapshots plus ordered committed events to the UI Projection Gateway.
Owned state: ephemeral connection/subscription generations, schema registry, bounded in-flight command map, and backpressure cursors; canonical command outcomes and projections are rebuilt from committed state.
Public commands/events and ports: accepts UiCommandV1 and ProjectionQueryV1 envelopes carrying commandId, expected target version, correlation, and typed payload; returns CommandReceiptV1, CommandRejectedV1, ProjectionSnapshotV1, ProjectionDeltaV1, and CoreEventEnvelopeV1. Dispatches Chat, workflow/configuration, credential, extension, approval, repair, evidence, and health intents to narrow core services.
Normative committed-stream contract: SubscribeCommitted(afterSequence) asynchronously sends only exact committed envelopes after the cursor. ProjectionSnapshot contains throughSequence, reducerVersion, stateHash, and reduced open/closed span state through that sequence; ProjectionDelta contains the exact missing committed envelopes. Live delivery is not a second event system and never substitutes a provisional event. A gap or reconnect recovers by exact delta or snapshot plus exact tail. Commit-to-delivery targets sub-100 ms feedback on supported local storage.

Invariants: only Aworkit DTOs cross the boundary; provider-, Rig-, database-, and OS-native types never cross it. Envelope acceptance is not domain success. The UI cannot invoke a capability, receive a secret, grant authority beyond a core decision, or commit state through this port.
Transactional and failure behavior: rejects malformed, unknown-version, stale-target, and oversized messages before delegation; same commandId is safe to resubmit and resolves through the durable command/event ledger. A gap or reconnect requires snapshot/delta resynchronization; slow subscribers are disconnected with a resumable cursor rather than blocking commits.
NFRs: target sub-50 ms validation/receipt latency, bounded memory, cancellation, structured diagnostics without sensitive payloads, and cross-platform Tauri parity.
Non-responsibilities: no view state, workflow execution, authority policy, persistence implementation, secret storage, or privileged side effects.

Concurrent desktop Chats (2026-09-15): Capture the explicit command target, reserve that Chat and execute in a blocking worker after releasing the coordinator lock. Queries, Settings, New Chat and selection stay available. Snapshots optionally address a Chat and otherwise resolve selected Chat. Project active Chat IDs and activity into history. Navigation and pinning use index semantics, independent of streaming Chat versions. Reject destructive/context-changing mutations only for an actively owned target. Late completion never changes selection.

Responsive windowed Chat loading (2026-09-16): Open only a bounded recent contiguous range of canonical events; fetch older ranges on upward scrolling. A window states its first sequence, head, and older-page cursor. Exact supporting events hydrate spans crossing the range boundary and their ancestors; they are explicitly separate from the contiguous range and never imply that omitted history was loaded. Preserve canonical IDs, payloads, duplicate/conflict validation, cursor fences, and immutable evidence. Render only activities belonging to the loaded range. Live delivery extends its head; gaps recover the exact missing tail. Navigation immediately selects a Chat shell with a local busy indicator, independently of persistence and data loading. Fence every result by Chat and navigation generation; stale loads cannot replace selection. Preserve drafts and scroll anchors when prepending. Queries, loading, schema upgrades and database access run on workers; never wait on the native UI thread. Long queries release the shared command coordinator and use independent read connections. Keep navigation and other Chats usable during all loading.
